name: Mississippi
agency: Mississippi Department of Public Safety, Driver Service Bureau
permitAge: 15 (Driver's License Manual p13; DPS Learner's Permit page). A 14-year-old enrolled in a school driver education class can get an instruction permit for driver education (DPS form DE-7, rev 04/2022).

teen.holdPermit: 12 months (manual p13, p15; DPS Learner's Permit page). Applicants 17 or older need not hold it 12 months.
teen.nightLimit: Not in the manual. The intermediate license was removed from law by 2021 HB 550 (signed 2021-04-05, per BillTrack50; official bill text not reachable), which also amended 63-1-21 on unsupervised driving by regular licensees under 18. Current hours unconfirmed.
teen.phone: All drivers: no writing, sending or reading texts, and no social media on a hand-held phone while driving; voice-operated and hands-free devices are excluded (manual p23).

notes: Handbook: Mississippi Driver's License Manual, 'Revised December 2024' (posted as 1.15.2025 Revised MDPS Driver's Manual, PDF modified Feb 2025). Printed page numbers match PDF pages.
Learner's permit at 15; licensed driver 21+ in the seat next to the learner; permit valid 2 years (p13).
50 hours of witnessed driving, certified by affidavit from a parent, teacher or guardian (p10, p13, p15, p17); under 17 this affidavit waives the road test.
Driver's education will be required for a new regular license from July 1, 2027 (p10, p15, p16; DPS news 2026-06-25).

The manual does not mention an intermediate license, night hours or passenger limits. Path: permit at 15, held one year, regular license (Class R) at 16 (p13, p15). The intermediate license was removed by 2021 HB 550 (third-party summary; official text not reachable). The 14-year-old driver-ed instruction permit is on DPS form DE-7.

Exam: computerized, with a headset that reads questions aloud (p17). Number of questions (30) and pass mark (24, 80%) come from third-party sites only; not on an official page. Test languages not stated.
Speed (p41): interstates 70 max, 40 min; four-lane state/US highways 65; two-lane 55; Natchez Trace 50; school zone 15.
Move over (p67): emergency vehicle parked on a four-lane highway: change lanes if safe, else slow and prepare to stop. Wider vehicle list and fines (Miss. Code 63-3-809) not in the manual.
School bus (p58): stop at least 10 feet away; on a divided highway with 2+ lanes each way, opposite direction may continue; same direction stops. Fines not in the manual.
Right on red after full stop unless signed (p37); left on red not in the manual.
